title: [mclag] After receiving the SAI_FDB_EVENT_MOVE event, the MAC address, which was originally learned from a remote MCLAG peer, cannot be aged out.
author: puffc
body:
**Description:** On non-Broadcom platforms like Innovium TL7, the fdborch receives the SAI_FDB_EVENT_MOVE event from SAI. However, based on our observations, the fdborch fails to update the MAC address type from static to dynamic and also neglects to update the allow_move attribute to false for MAC addresses originally learned from MCLAG peers. **Steps to reproduce the issue:** 1. Configure the MCLAG topology. 2. Transmit a packet to the orphan port connected to the second MCLAG switch. 3. Transmit a packet with the same MAC address to the MCLAG port-channel connected to the first MCLAG switch. 4. Verify the status of the MAC address in the MAC address table of the first MCLAG switch. **Describe the results you received:** The following is captured from the first MCLAG switch: 1. Before receiving the mac movement event: 
admin@sonic:~$ show mac
  No.    Vlan  MacAddress         Port          Type
-----  ------  -----------------  ------------  -------
    1      10  7C:C2:55:4A:48:96  Ethernet16    Dynamic
    2    1000  00:10:94:00:00:AA  PortChannel2  Static   --> Static type
    3    1000  0C:48:C6:86:16:8A  PortChannel1  Dynamic
    4    1000  00:25:90:B2:C7:F7  PortChannel2  Static
Total number of entries 4

IVM-R>ifcs show l2_entry
Total l2_entry count: 4
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  key_type |          mac_addr | mac_mask | source | group |        l2vni |     entry_dest | entry_type |       fwd_policy |       ctc_policy | user_cookie | hitbit |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| mac_l2vni | 00:25:90:b2:c7:f7 |       *  |     *  |    *  | (l2vni:1000) |     (lag:   2) |     STATIC | ('0', 'FORWARD') | ('0', 'DISABLE') |           0 |      0 |
| mac_l2vni | 00:10:94:00:00:aa |       *  |     *  |    *  | (l2vni:1000) |     (lag:   2) |     STATIC | ('0', 'FORWARD') | ('0', 'DISABLE') |           0 |      0 |  --> static type
| mac_l2vni | 0c:48:c6:86:16:8a |       *  |     *  |    *  | (l2vni:1000) |     (lag:   1) |    DYNAMIC | ('0', 'FORWARD') | ('0', 'DISABLE') |           0 |      0 |
| mac_l2vni | 7c:c2:55:4a:48:96 |       *  |     *  |    *  | (l2vni:  10) | (sysport: 225) |    DYNAMIC | ('0', 'FORWARD') | ('0', 'DISABLE') |           0 |      1 |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
Total l2_entry count: 4
2. After receiving the mac movement event: 
admin@sonic:~$ show mac
  No.    Vlan  MacAddress         Port          Type
-----  ------  -----------------  ------------  -------
    1      10  7C:C2:55:4A:48:96  Ethernet16    Dynamic
    2    1000  00:10:94:00:00:AA  PortChannel1  Dynamic   ---> Dynamic type
    3    1000  7E:C2:55:4A:48:96  PortChannel2  Dynamic
    4    1000  0C:48:C6:86:16:8A  PortChannel1  Dynamic
    5    1000  7C:C2:55:4A:48:96  PortChannel2  Dynamic
    6    1000  00:25:90:B2:C7:F7  PortChannel2  Static
Total number of entries 6

IVM-R>exit
admin@sonic:~$ mclagdctl dump mac -i 1
TYPE: S-STATIC, D-DYNAMIC; AGE: L-Local age, P-Peer age
No.   TYPE MAC                 VID  DEV                 ORIGIN-DEV          AGE
1     D    7c:c2:55:4a:48:96   10   PortChannel2        PortChannel2        L
2     D    00:10:94:00:00:aa   1000 PortChannel1        PortChannel1        P   ---> PeerAge (local learn)
3     D    00:25:90:b2:c7:f7   1000 PortChannel2        Ethernet256         L
4     D    0c:48:c6:86:16:8a   1000 PortChannel1        PortChannel1        P
admin@sonic:~$


IVM-R>ifcs show l2_entry
Total l2_entry count: 6
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  key_type |          mac_addr | mac_mask | source | group |        l2vni |     entry_dest | entry_type |       fwd_policy |       ctc_policy | user_cookie | hitbit |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| mac_l2vni | 00:25:90:b2:c7:f7 |       *  |     *  |    *  | (l2vni:1000) |     (lag:   2) |     STATIC | ('0', 'FORWARD') | ('0', 'DISABLE') |           0 |      0 |
| mac_l2vni | 00:10:94:00:00:aa |       *  |     *  |    *  | (l2vni:1000) |     (lag:   1) |     STATIC | ('0', 'FORWARD') | ('0', 'DISABLE') |           0 |      0 |  --> Static Type on po1
| mac_l2vni | 7e:c2:55:4a:48:96 |       *  |     *  |    *  | (l2vni:1000) |     (lag:   2) |    DYNAMIC | ('0', 'FORWARD') | ('0', 'DISABLE') |           0 |      0 |
| mac_l2vni | 0c:48:c6:86:16:8a |       *  |     *  |    *  | (l2vni:1000) |     (lag:   1) |    DYNAMIC | ('0', 'FORWARD') | ('0', 'DISABLE') |           0 |      0 |
| mac_l2vni | 7c:c2:55:4a:48:96 |       *  |     *  |    *  | (l2vni:  10) | (sysport: 225) |    DYNAMIC | ('0', 'FORWARD') | ('0', 'DISABLE') |           0 |      1 |
| mac_l2vni | 7c:c2:55:4a:48:96 |       *  |     *  |    *  | (l2vni:1000) |     (lag:   2) |    DYNAMIC | ('0', 'FORWARD') | ('0', 'DISABLE') |           0 |      1 |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Fixes sonic-net/sonic-swss#2810

**What I did**
After receiving the MAC address movement event from the hardware, update the MAC address type from static to dynamic and also update the allow_move attribute to false if the MAC address was originally learned from the remote MCLAG peer.

**Why I did it**
To fix the hardware MAC address update problem as stated in the description.

**How I verified it**
Passed all mclag UT and also verfied on the Innovium TL7 platform.
